questions.question:
**Direction: Improve the underlined part of the sentence. Choose ‘No improvement’ as an answer if the sentence is grammatically correct.**

The final cost depends on whether you **__chooses the small__** or the large size.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **"choose the small."**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The error lies in the part **"chooses the small."**
 
• **"You"** is always definite even when it is not specific.
 
• Semantically, **"you"** is both singular and plural, though syntactically it is always plural.
 
• It always takes a verb form that originally marked the word as plural.
 
• The verb** 'choose' **should be in the present tense to match the subject** 'you'.**
 
 
• **Example**: *You **are**__ a nice person.*
 
 
 
• The correct answer is Option 2.

 

**Correct sentence**: *The final cost depends on whether you __**choose the small**__ or the large size.*

questions.question:
A sentence has been given with a blank to be filled with an appropriate option. Choose the correct alternative.

Neither she ______ I have expected Reema’s arrival.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is "**nor**."

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **"Nor" is used to introduce a second negative clause, following neither, indicating that the second option is not true either. **
 
• "Neither" is a negative conjunction that is used to introduce two negative alternatives.
 
• "Nor" is the appropriate option to complete the sentence as it is the negative counterpart of "or".
 
• In case of the given sentence, both the person did not know about the arrival of Reema.
 
• The correct sentence should read:
 
 
• "Neither she nor I have expected Reema's arrival."
 
 

Hence, **the correct answer is option 3**.

• Option 2 (along) is not the correct option as it does not make sense in the given context.
 
• Option 4 (or) is not the correct option as it is a positive conjunction that introduces a choice between two alternatives.
